detail.longDescription: I have a function that takes one or more arguments and returns the same number of values. For a single input value, it returns just one value, not a size one tuple, for multiple values it returns a tuple whose length corresponds to the number if input values. def foo(val: int, *more_vals: int) -> str | tuple[str, ...]: out = tuple(str(v) for v in (val, *more_vals)) if not more_vals: out, = out return out How do I correctly type-hint this behavior using @overload ? In particular, I want to hint that the return value is a tuple only for multiple input values. (The fact that the tuple has the same number of values as the input is less important.) The single-value case is clear: @overload def foo(val: int) -> str: ... What's unclear is how I hint the multi-argument case. Both of these tries cause Pylance to complain: @overload def foo(val: int, *more_vals: int) -> tuple[str, ...]: ... # Overlaps with single-argument case. @overload def foo(val: int, val2: int, *more_vals: int) -> tuple[str, ...]: ... # Not consistent with implementation.
